nil.lede: The rules changed fast, and they now cover recruits too. Here's what's true for you this year.
cards: Your first deal is still open
You're committed, not signed. Until signing day in December, the terms of your first college agreement are still on the table.
You can have an agent now
Starting in 2026-27, NCAA rules let recruits hire agents before they enroll and keep their eligibility, for every part of the deal, including revenue share with the school.
Schools can pay players directly, up to $21.3 million per school this year. What a freshman lineman gets, and on what terms, is negotiated.
The IHSAA now allows NIL deals, but no school name, logo or uniform, and your school must be told within 48 hours. Break those and you can lose eligibility.
Buyouts, transfer clauses, what happens if you get hurt or the staff changes. Ryan reads every line before anything is signed.

parentQA.q: He's already committed. Why does he need anyone?
parentQA.a: Committed isn't signed. The terms of his first agreement with Indiana are negotiated, and starting this year NCAA rules let recruits have an agent for that. We make sure the deal matches the commitment. We have no interest in changing his school.

parentQA.q: Is this allowed for a high schooler?
parentQA.a: Yes. Starting in 2026-27, NCAA rules let recruits hire agents before they enroll and keep their eligibility. In Indiana, the IHSAA allows NIL deals as long as there's no school name, logo or uniform, and the school is told within 48 hours.
Nothing up front. The fee is written into the agreement before anything is signed, and we walk you through it in person.
